Open Start and type your agency name and your rules in the yellow cells: pace limits, the most times a person should see an ad, the fall in click rate that means a tired ad, days before a tracking recheck and the return you aim for.
List each client in Ad Clients with the monthly ad budget and your fee rate. Spend, leads, return, balance and the days of money left fill in by themselves.
Record each ad account in Ad Accounts and each campaign in Campaigns with its daily budget and dates; build its Ad Sets and Ads and Creatives under it.
Add one row a week for each campaign in Weekly Spend. The pace against plan and a flag for overspending or underspending appear at once.
Add one row a month for each campaign in Results with the impressions, clicks, leads, sales and revenue from the platform. Cost per result, click-through rate and return fill in.
Set a monthly budget for each client in Budget Plan and watch the share used. Record every payment from a client in Budget Top-Ups so the balance is right.
Work out your management fee each month in Management Fees and mark it billed when you invoice it.
Check Tracking Checks, Landing Pages and Lead Forms before you raise a budget, and run Audience Tests and Retargeting to find audiences with a lower cost per lead.
Watch Creative Fatigue each week and log every platform decision in Ad Reviews so repeated rejection reasons are found.
Compare your real costs with your targets in Cost Per Result and note the promo codes in Promo Codes.
Use the 14 calculators for the budget split, cost per result, return, break-even cost, pacing, frequency, fatigue, lead value, forecast, test size, fees, scaling, top-ups and promo codes.
Read Paid Ads Dashboard and Charts every week: spend, pace, balances, cost per lead, return, fatigue, rejections and fees.
Run creator campaigns, contracts and payments for every brand you manage
Creator database with a fair price check

every creator you approach has a stage, a gap between offer and ask and a warning when a message is waiting too long
contracts add up against the budget of each campaign, with money paid, money left and the cost for 1000 people reached
paid use, partner ad use and buyout fees are worked out from the creator fee, with the date the rights end
overlapping periods for the same creator and niche are flagged before you sign a second brand
every post a creator owes shows its due date, the days late and the days an approval waits
Payments to creators with overdue warnings
deposits and final payments show paid, due soon, late and overdue, with the money still owed on every contract
reach, reactions, engagement rate, cost for each engagement and cost for 1000 people reached are worked out for each creator post
clicks, orders and sales become commission, discount cost, sales for each unit spent and net result
each live post is checked for the ad label, a clear first line, the brand tag and honest claims, with a pass mark
the suspicious share and the audience country give the real followers and the real cost for 1000 followers

One row for each brand; campaigns, budget, money committed to creators and sales from codes fill in from the other pages.
One row for each creator with followers, engagement and asking rate; the fair price from the rate card, the cost for 1000 views, jobs, earnings and your own score fill in.
Rate card benchmarks by platform and creator size
One row for each platform and creator size with the low and high price for one post; the typical price, the creators you know there and what they ask on average fill in.
Outreach pipeline: from first message to agreement
One row for each creator you approach for a brand with the stage, dates, your offer and their ask; the days open, the gap and a follow-up warning fill in.
One row for each creator campaign with its goal, dates and budget; the creators, money committed and paid, what is left, the reach and the cost for 1000 people fill in.
One row for each creator contract with the fee, the posts and the usage rights; the usage fee, exclusivity fee, total, agency fee, usage end date and money still owed fill in.
Deliverables tracker: every post a creator owes
One row for each post a creator must publish with its due date and the date it went live; the days late, the brand and an on time check fill in.
Content approvals before a post goes live
One row for each draft sent for approval with the dates and rounds; the days waiting, the due date of the post and whether the answer came in time fill in.
One row for each payment you owe a creator with the due and paid dates; the days late, the campaign and whether it is paid, due soon or overdue fill in.
Gifted products and the posts they bring
One row for each product sent to a creator with its value and result; the days since sending, the brand and a chase reminder fill in.
One row for each code or tracked link a creator shares with its clicks, orders and sales; the commission, the sales for each unit spent and the net result fill in.
One row for each live post with its reach and reactions; the engagement rate, the cost of the post, the cost for each engagement and for 1000 people reached fill in.
Brand fit scores for each creator and brand
One row for each creator and brand you judge on audience, values, style and brand safety from 1 to 10; the weighted score and a fit verdict fill in.
One row for each period in which a creator may not work with rival brands; the length, days left and any clash with another brand in the same niche fill in.
Disclosure checks: is the ad label on every post
One row for each live post you check for an ad label, a clear first line, a brand tag and honest claims; the checks passed and the verdict fill in.
One row for each event where a creator appears with the fee, travel, guests and leads; the total cost, cost for each lead and days to go fill in.
One row for each creator who represents a brand for months with a monthly fee and a post target; the end date, progress, cost for each post and a behind-target flag fill in.
One row for each audit of a creator with the share of suspicious followers and the audience in your target country; the real followers, the real cost for 1000 and a verdict fill in.
Feedback about each creator after a campaign
One row for each creator after a campaign, scored 1 to 5 on replies, quality, timing and ease of work; the average and a rating fill in.

Hi {name}, we love your content and would like to work with you for {brand}. Can we send you a short brief and our offer?
Hi {name}, a quick follow up on our message {days_open} days ago about a paid collaboration for {brand}. Are you open to it?
Hi {name}, our offer for {brand} is {offer}. Your ask is {ask}. Can we meet in the middle?
Hi {name}, your contract {ct_id} for {brand} is ready: {posts} posts for {fee}, total {total} with the rights. Please sign and send it back.
Hi {name}, the usage rights in contract {ct_id} for {brand} end on {usage_end} ({days_left} days). Do you agree to extend them?
Hi {name}, for contract {ct_id} we still owe you {owed}. We will pay it on the agreed date.
Hi {name}, your post "{title}" for {brand} is due on {due} ({days_left} days). Can you confirm the date?
Hi {name}, the post "{title}" for {brand} was due on {due}. Can you post today and send us the link?
Thank you {name}, the post "{title}" is live. Please send us the reach and the reactions from your own numbers.
Hi {name}, we checked your draft "{title}" for {brand}. It is on round {rounds}. We will send our comments today.
Hi {name}, the draft "{title}" has waited {days_wait} days for approval. The post is due on {post_due}. We are chasing the client.
Hi {name}, your draft "{title}" is approved. You can post on {post_due}. Please keep the ad label in the first line.
Hi {name}, we paid {amount} ({kind}) for contract {contract}. Please confirm that it arrived.
Hi {name}, your {kind} of {amount} is due on {due}. Please check that your bank details are still correct.
Hi {name}, sorry, your {kind} of {amount} was due on {due}. We are paying it today.
Hi {name}, we sent you {product} ({qty} items) from {brand}. Please tell us when it arrives.
Hi {name}, it has been {days} days since we sent {product}. Did it arrive? We would love to see a post, with the ad label.
Hi {name}, your post "{title}" for {brand} passed {score} of 4 ad label checks. Please add a clear ad label in the first line today.
Hi {name}, your post "{title}" passed our ad label check. Thank you for the clear label.
Hi {name}, you are booked for the {kind} on {date} at {place} for {brand}. The fee is {fee}. Please confirm.
Hi {name}, a reminder: the event at {place} is in {days} days ({date}). Please send us your arrival time.
Hi {name}, you have posted {posts_done} times for {brand} and we planned {posts_month} each month. Can we plan the next posts?
Thank you {name} for {elapsed} months as an ambassador for {brand}. Your code {code} is working well.
Hi {name}, could you send screenshots of your audience statistics (countries, age and followers by day)? We need them to finish our check.
Hi {name}, thank you for the campaign for {brand}. We scored the work {avg} out of 5.
Hi {name}, would you like to work with us again for {brand}? We enjoyed the last campaign.
Hi, update for "{name}" ({brand}): {live} of {posts} posts are live and reached {reach} people. Budget left: {left}.
Hi {name}, we have a new campaign for a {niche} brand. Are you free next month? Your usual rate for a post is {rate}.
Hi, for {brand}: {campaigns} creator campaigns, {committed} committed to creators and {revenue} in sales from codes.

Open Start and type your agency name and your own rules in the yellow cells: your fee, the fees for usage rights and exclusivity, the engagement you call good and the weights for fit.
Fill Brand Clients with one row for each brand. Campaigns, budget, money committed to creators and sales from codes fill in from the other pages.
Keep Rate Card up to date with the low and high price for a post on every platform and creator size. The typical price and the average ask of your creators fill in.
Add every creator on Creators with followers, engagement rate and asking rate. The price check tells you at once if the rate is above or below the rate card.
Track every creator you approach on Outreach Pipeline. The next step shows who needs a follow up, and the gap shows how far your offer is from their ask.
Write each campaign on Campaign Briefs with its budget, then record each creator agreement on Contracts. Usage fee, exclusivity fee, your fee, the usage end date and the money still owed fill in.
List every post a creator owes on Deliverables and every draft on Content Approvals. Days late, days waiting and the status fill in.
Record every deposit and final payment on Creator Payments. Overdue payments, money owed and the days late fill in.
Score each live post on Creator Results with its reach and reactions to see the engagement rate, the cost for each engagement and the cost for 1000 people reached.
Add each code or tracked link on Codes and Links to see commission, discount cost, sales for each unit spent and the net result.
Use Brand Fit, Follower Audits, Ad Label Checks and Exclusivity before you sign and after each post, and Creator Feedback after each campaign.
Use Gifted Products, Event Appearances and Ambassadors for the other ways you work with creators.

Use the 14 calculators for rates, cost per engagement, return, fit, commission, usage rights, payment schedules, budget split, reach, gifting, exclusivity, shortlists, real audience cost and ambassadors.
Read Creators Dashboard and Charts every week: overdue posts and payments, usage rights ending, ad label checks, budget and results.
